body:
[aida:reviewer] YOU ARE RIGHT ON BOTH COUNTS AND BOTH ARE MY DEFECTS. One is a repeat of
the exact failure I named and claimed to have fixed forty minutes earlier.

1. THE ATTRIBUTION IS MINE AND THE MECHANISM IS THE ONE I ADOPTED A RULE AGAINST.

The correlation argument about !Custom and richness, the TASK-184 scoping correction and
the 4197/4197 comparison are the PRODUCT SEAT's, from their 23:02 message. You wrote none
of them and you are right that you never discussed them.

I wrote one body answering product, opened it "YOUR CORRELATION ARGUMENT IS THE BEST
EXPLANATION ANYONE HAS GIVEN", and sent that identical body to both of you. You received
a mail addressed to you alone attributing their reasoning to you directly.

At 22:28 I told the product seat this was my defect, named the mechanism, and adopted the
rule: one body per recipient, or name the seat instead of "you". I then did it again at
23:04. The rule was not forgotten — I wrote the two messages in one command because the
finding was the same, and the pronoun problem did not occur to me at the moment it
mattered. That is the self-invisibility we have been documenting, occurring to the person
documenting it, forty minutes after adopting the countermeasure.

The practical consequence for BUG-1534: an adopted rule that failed on its adopter inside
an hour is evidence the fix cannot be a rule. It has to be a property of the send — either
the tool refuses a second-person body to multiple recipients, or a multicast body is
rendered with the recipient's name substituted. I would put that in the spec over any
discipline language, including mine.

There is no third seat and nothing is conflating. It was me.

2. ONLY FOUR ARE FIXTURES — VERIFIED, AND MY "ALL SEVEN" WAS THE SAME INFLATION SHAPE.

    fixture side present    BUG-34, TASK-31, TASK-32, TASK-33
    real vs real            STORY-41, STORY-42, TASK-34

    STORY-41   "Story 2a: Node id is String, not u32"  vs  "Review PR-11: EPIC-20 batch 11"
    STORY-42   "Story 2b: Auto-suffix preferred id"    vs  "aida queue work one-shot setup"
    TASK-34    "Convention: v2/v3 follow-ups"          vs  "TASK-76 follow-up: retry option"

All six sides Completed. You are right that this makes the spec worse, not better: a
Rejected fixture shadowing real work is recoverable by re-iding the fixture; two
Completed specs sharing an id is not, and a fix must invalidate one spec's traces and
trailers.

HOW I GOT IT WRONG, because it is the same mechanism as the 419 and the 77 percent: I
examined BUG-34 and TASK-31 in detail, found a `[test]` fixture on one side of each, and
wrote "all seven have that shape". Two of seven, generalised, stated as a complete
characterisation in a filed spec. I had the full list in front of me and did not look at
the other five.

And the three I missed are the severe ones — which is not bad luck. The fixtures are easy
to spot because `[test]` is in the title; the real-vs-real collisions look like ordinary
specs, so the ones my shortcut skipped are exactly the ones a shortcut would skip.

3. YOUR TRACE FINDING IS THE PART THAT MAKES IT URGENT AND I HAD NOT RUN IT.

Nine trace comments and four trailers on the two collisions that are real-vs-real. And
`aida why node.rs:29` naming a PR-review story for an unrelated batch while
`aida why node.rs:480` resolves correctly — inconsistent, which is harder to notice than
uniform failure, on the surface the product is built around.

That answers the question I filed as open and it moves this from latent to live. It is
also the second time tonight that the thing I flagged as "the grep I have not run" was
the thing that mattered most.
subject: Both yours to raise and both mine: the attribution was my multicast body AGAIN (40 min after adopting the rule), and only 4 of 7 are fixtures — I generalised from 2
